status: OPEN FINDING — discovered during M52H, NOT fixed here (out of scope); needs its own investigation
symptom: the production stt-runtime SERVICE path returned unstable, truncated Hindi transcripts on a 31.8 s real multi-speaker clip (real30s.wav) while every DIRECT call to the very same llama-server child was stable and complete

isolation_matrix_real30s.service_/v1/transcribe_x7: 77 / 33 / 71 / 31 / 96 / 2 / 65 words, inference 20.7-45.3 s, WER vs truth 0.60-1.00 — UNSTABLE run to run at temperature 0.0 (also reproduced after a fresh container restart)
isolation_matrix_real30s.direct_child_same_container_x3_ffmpeg_de: 117 words each, 6.7-9.1 s — stable (rules out the audio path: ffmpeg decode + wav_bytes wrap are byte-innocent)
isolation_matrix_real30s.child_slots_probe_after_service_call: n_prompt_tokens 899 — the FULL audio reaches the child through the service too

what_is_ruled_out: backend/build (Windows CPU, Linux CPU, CUDA all stable-full on direct calls)
payload shape (engine payload mirrored exactly in the stable direct tests)
child crash/restart (runtime logs clean, same child pid across good and bad results)
max_tokens (2048 in engine; truncations far below it)
hypothesis_UNCONFIRMED: CPU contention inside the runtime process (uvicorn + worker pool + resident whisper) changes llama.cpp's thread work-splitting, whose floating-point reduction order is not deterministic under load; on knife-edge audio the greedy path diverges — sometimes into early stop. Consistent with: service inference 2-5x slower than direct on the same clip, instability appearing only via the service, and this morning's short single-speaker prefix ladder through the SAME service being stable.
why_it_never_showed_before: every prior Hindi battery used short single-clip audio (FLEURS/IndicVoices single utterances, <=20 s, one speaker); real30s is the first 30 s multi-speaker concat pushed through the service
impact_on_m52h: none on the GPU verdict (GPU + all direct paths stable); CPU-vs-GPU quality was therefore scored with DIRECT child calls on both sides
impact_on_production: potentially real for long multi-speaker uploads on CPU-contended boxes — recommend a dedicated investigation milestone (repro on the production-shaped box, llama.cpp --threads pinning, batch-order determinism)
